title: Coherent lattice dynamics distinguish Holstein and Su-Schrieffer-Heeger electron-phonon coupling
authors: Debshikha Banerjee, Jinu Thomas, G. Alvarez, T. P. Devereaux, T. A. Maier, S. Johnston
abstract: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy provides a powerful means to investigate electron-phonon (e-ph) interactions in strongly correlated systems. Nevertheless, the question of how different microscopic e-ph coupling mechanisms influence the lattice's nonequilibrium response has not been widely addressed. We perform time-dependent density matrix renormalization group simulations on a pumped one-dimensional Mott insulator coupled to phonons through either Holstein or Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) interactions. The electronic responses of the two models are qualitatively similar in the Mott-insulating regime and are governed by the same excitations and resonance conditions of the Hubbard model. In contrast, the lattice dynamics of the two models differ substantially. While the Hubbard-Holstein model exhibits long-lived coherent phonon oscillations when the pump resonates with the bare phonon frequency, no such oscillations are observed for the Hubbard-SSH model. These contrasting responses remain robust against changes in phonon frequency and pump parameters, suggesting that coherent lattice dynamics can provide a direct nonequilibrium probe of the microscopic form of e-ph coupling.
summary: This work uses time-dependent DMRG simulations to compare the non-equilibrium response of two electron-phonon coupling models: Holstein and Su-Schrieffer-Heeger. The authors find that while electronic measurements fail to distinguish the couplings, the resulting coherent lattice dynamics provide a robust signature, showing distinct phonon oscillations for the Holstein model versus none for the SSH model.
main_problem: To determine if coherent lattice dynamics can distinguish between different microscopic electron-phonon (e-ph) coupling mechanisms (Holstein vs. Su-Schrieffer-Heeger) when the system is driven out of equilibrium.
main_result: While electronic responses are similar, the lattice dynamics differ substantially: the Holstein model shows long-lived coherent phonon oscillations, whereas the SSH model does not.
method: Time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations were used to calculate the time evolution of electronic and lattice observables following an ultrafast pump pulse.
model_or_system: The study investigates a one-dimensional Mott insulator coupled to phonons, comparing the Hubbard-Holstein (HH) model (local potential modulation) and the Hubbard-SSH (HSSH) model (hopping modulation).
key_observables: Lattice dynamics (e.g., $\Delta E_{	ext{ph}}$, $\Delta \hat{X}_{c	ext{disp}}$) and electronic observables ($\Delta E_{	ext{total}}$, $\Delta E_U$).
important_parameters: The system is analyzed in the Mott-insulating regime, with key parameters including the coupling strength ($\alpha$), phonon frequency ($\omega_{	ext{ph}}$), and pump frequency ($\omega_0$).
main_assumptions: The contrast in lattice dynamics is robust against changes in phonon frequency and pump parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the pump-induced electronic response ($\Delta E_{	ext{total}}$) showing qualitative similarity, contrasted by figures showing the lattice response, where HH exhibits clear coherent oscillations while HSSH does not.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem by comparing the Hamiltonians of HH and HSSH models. It then simulates the non-equilibrium dynamics using DMRG, showing that while electronic properties are insensitive to the coupling type, the resulting coherent lattice dynamics provide a clear, distinguishing signature.
why_interesting: The clear distinction in lattice dynamics provides a novel, measurable diagnostic tool for probing the microscopic nature of electron-phonon coupling in strongly correlated materials, which is highly relevant to understanding high-Tc superconductivity.
